subject: phoenix
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: phoenix with flame plumage, wings spread.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a moderately sized module for a phoenix model, deciding on a standing pose with wings spread outward and legs reaching the ground, keeping it concise but SDK-correct.

I'm structuring the skeleton with a hip root, spine chain running through chest/neck/head, a tail chain, limb-based legs, and wing chains with shoulder/elbow/wrist joints plus feather extrudes, while planning a Genshin-style palette using the toon kit's cel paint with crimson-to-orange-to-yellow gradients along each feather.

Defining spine path points...

I'm setting radii values for the body sweep to taper from fat belly to thin neck, and planning a countershaded cel paint with crimson-to-gold gradient. For the head, I'm sketching out the skull sphere, beak cones with a jaw joint, and eye decals placed on the skull surface.

Now I'm working out the crest feathers, a chain of tail joints with streaming feather extrudes at varying angles, and a reusable feather helper function for extruding outlines with thickness along cross directions. I'm also starting to position the wing shoulder joints symmetrically on each side.

Defining the wing arm chain and feather fan...

I'm adding small glowing flame wisps at the wing tips and tail ends for extra flair, plus a glowing ember gem on the chest. For the feather shape itself, I'm defining a pointed outline tapering to a sharp tip and writing a paint function that blends crimson to orange along the feather's length based on position.

Now I'm working out the leg geometry, defining hip-to-foot positions and segment lengths for thigh and shin bends so the legs articulate naturally.

Adjusting foot height so toes just touch the floor without sinking. Now working out the body and spine proportions, setting hip height and body sweep radius, then building a tail bone chain extending backward from the root.

I'm fanning out tail feathers in a horizontal arc with drooping angles across two layers, then defining the spine chain starting at the root joint, and setting up a head joint attached to the end of the spine pointing forward.

Now I'm plotting the neck's path with a curve of points rising from the base to the head, placing the skull as a slightly elongated sphere offset forward from the head joint, and shaping the beak as a tapered spike extending forward and down from the skull.

I'm defining the lower jaw as a shorter, thinner spike bone positioned just below the upper beak, giving the beak a gold flat color. Then I'm figuring out how to place eye decals on the skull's surface using surface hit detection, mirroring them left and right based on the side parameter.

Now I'm working out the crest feathers—five of them extending back and up from the head bone, varying their lateral directions, and thinking through which axes should define each feather's width versus thickness so they sit correctly in a vertical plane.

I'm also deciding whether to add chest ember glow, a collar ruff, or a ring of small neck feathers, but leaning toward keeping it simple using the existing spine curve. Now I'm starting to write a reusable fan helper for the wings, setting up the chain of bone names from shoulder through elbow to wrist.

Continuing the wing rig...

Writing feather helper function...

Defining body and leg colors with countershading, then shaping the spine's radius profile along the chain so the body is fatter toward the chest and tapers near the tail base.

Sweeping the tail geometry and adding layered feather fans radiating outward at varying angles and lengths, with a shorter gold layer and glowing tips on top before finalizing the crest and feet.
